title: “which vail is done away in Christ” (2 Corinthians 3:14) — Tischendorf’s Greek has a word meaning “because” and adds “this very day”
summary: KJV 2 Corinthians 3:14 ends “which vail is done away in Christ”, with the veil as the thing removed. The Textus Receptus text served prints ο τι εν χριστω καταργειται; Tischendorf’s text prints ὅτι ἐν Χριστῷ καταργεῖται and, earlier in the verse, τῆς σήμερον ἡμέρας [this very day], where the TR text has της σημερον.
text: KJV 2 Corinthians 3:14: “But their minds were blinded: for until this day remaineth the same vail untaken away in the reading of the old testament; which vail is done away in Christ.” Greek New Testament (Tischendorf, eighth edition) 2 Corinthians 3:14: ἀλλὰ ἐπωρώθη τὰ νοήματα αὐτῶν. ἄχρι γὰρ τῆς σήμερον ἡμέρας τὸ αὐτὸ κάλυμμα ἐπὶ τῇ ἀναγνώσει τῆς παλαιᾶς διαθήκης μένει μὴ ἀνακαλυπτόμενον, ὅτι ἐν Χριστῷ καταργεῖται· Greek New Testament (Textus Receptus as served, printed there without accents) 2 Corinthians 3:14: αλλ επωρωθη τα νοηματα αυτων αχρι γαρ της σημερον το αυτο καλυμμα επι τη αναγνωσει της παλαιας διαθηκης μενει μη ανακαλυπτομενον ο τι εν χριστω καταργειται Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/TISCH/47/3/ and https://bolls.life/get-text/TR/47/3/.
reasoning: The two editions divide the words differently at the end of the verse: ο τι (“which”) in the TR text served, ὅτι (“because” or “that”) in Tischendorf. With ὅτι the clause gives the reason the veil is not lifted, namely that it is taken away only in Christ; with ο τι the veil itself is the thing taken away in Christ. Tischendorf’s text also adds ἡμέρας after τῆς σήμερον.
scope: T applies at 2 Corinthians 3:14 only. The difference is between Greek editions: the Textus Receptus text served agrees with the KJV and Tischendorf’s text does not. title: “our care for you” (2 Corinthians 7:12) — Tischendorf’s Greek has “your care for us”
summary: KJV 2 Corinthians 7:12 says Paul wrote so that “our care for you” might appear. The Textus Receptus text served prints την σπουδην ημων την υπερ υμων [our care on behalf of you]; Tischendorf’s text prints τὴν σπουδὴν ὑμῶν τὴν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν [your care on behalf of us].

title: “comforted in your comfort” (2 Corinthians 7:13) — Tischendorf’s Greek has “our comfort” and starts a new sentence
summary: KJV 2 Corinthians 7:13 begins “Therefore we were comforted in your comfort”. The Textus Receptus text served prints επι τη παρακλησει υμων [in your comfort]; Tischendorf’s text prints ἐπὶ δὲ τῇ παρακλήσει ἡμῶν [and in our comfort] after a stop, so that the sentence “we have been comforted” ends and a new one begins.

reasoning: Both the pronoun and the sentence division differ: υμων (your) against ἡμῶν (our), and no δέ in the TR text against δέ in Tischendorf’s. title: “whereof ye had notice before” (2 Corinthians 9:5) — Tischendorf’s Greek has “promised beforehand”
summary: KJV 2 Corinthians 9:5 has the bounty “whereof ye had notice before”. The Textus Receptus text served prints προκατηγγελμενην [announced beforehand]; Tischendorf’s text prints προεπηγγελμένην [promised beforehand].
text: KJV 2 Corinthians 9:5: “Therefore I thought it necessary to exhort the brethren, that they would go before unto you, and make up beforehand your bounty, whereof ye had notice before, that the same might be ready, as a matter of bounty, and not as of covetousness.” Greek New Testament (Tischendorf, eighth edition) 2 Corinthians 9:5: ἀναγκαῖον οὖν ἡγησάμην παρακαλέσαι τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς ἵνα προέλθωσιν εἰς ὑμᾶς καὶ προκαταρτίσωσιν τὴν προεπηγγελμένην εὐλογίαν ὑμῶν, ταύτην ἑτοίμην εἶναι οὕτως ὡς εὐλογίαν, μὴ ὡς πλεονεξίαν. title: “minister bread … multiply … increase” (2 Corinthians 9:10) — Tischendorf’s Greek has future-tense verbs
summary: KJV 2 Corinthians 9:10 reads as a wish or prayer: “minister bread … multiply your seed … increase the fruits”. title: “which the Lord hath given us” (2 Corinthians 10:8) — Tischendorf’s Greek has no “us” and a future verb for “boast”
